content.text: No reciprocal Corio indemnity exists, and Section 9 expressly carves Section 8 liability out of the cap, so the Vendor indemnity is uncapped. Submitting as compliant at the fallback.

input.quote: Commerce One shall indemnify, defend and hold harmless Corio and its Customers from any and all damages, liabilities, costs and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees) incurred by Corio or its Customers arising out of any claim that the Software infringes any patent, copyright, trademark or trade right secret of a third party
input.rationale: Section 8.1 sits at (and in places above) the fallback position: Commerce One expressly defends, indemnifies and holds Corio and its Customers harmless against third-party claims that the Software infringes patent, copyright, trademark or trade secret rights; the usual procedure (prompt notice, tender of control, cooperation) is present; and the remedy ladder is complete — procure the right to continue use, replace or modify, and failing those, terminate and refund a pro-rated portion of fees paid. The exclusions in Section 8.2 (use outside the Documentation; third-party modification) are within the permitted fallback exclusions and are in fact narrower than the fallback allows (no combination or specification carve-outs). No super-cap is needed because Section 9 expressly excludes "LIABILITY ARISING UNDER SECTION 8" from both the 12-month fees cap and the consequential-damages exclusion, leaving the indemnity uncapped — better for us than a 3x annual fees super-cap. There is no Corio indemnity anywhere in the Agreement, so there is no one-way exposure to narrow. Short of the preferred position, the indemnity does not extend to Commerce One's breach of applicable law, a Commerce One-caused data breach, or its gross negligence/wilful misconduct, and covers "Corio and its Customers" rather than affiliates; we note these as upside items only and do not redline a clause that meets the fallback on its material terms.
